source_title: Root: A Game of Woodland Might and Right
continuity_scope: Terms-only audit bound to the 2018 first printing of Leder Games' Root base board game. Leder Games identifies Root as released in 2018. Current product/resources and the Oct. 2025 Law of Root are used only to identify enduring terminology and later rules hierarchy; they do not silently replace this first-printing witness. Third printing introduced corrections and minor faction-board balance adjustments, so later printings and current Law text remain separate rules witnesses.
work_or_witnesses: Root: A Game of Woodland Might and Right, Leder Games, first printing, 2018
Leder Games Rules Library: Law of Root, updated October 8, 2025 (later rules witness)
coverage_rule: Include a named individual only where the first-printing core directly profiles a stable dramatic person. Marquise de Cat, Eyrie Dynasties, Woodland Alliance, and Vagabond are player-selected faction/role systems; their boards, leaders, and classes are not character nodes. The available official core material profiles asymmetric play systems and a variable contest, not named people. No individual qualifies.
omissions: All expansions, hirelings, landmark/deck packs, Clockwork bots, later maps, current 2025 Homeland material, and their names or story claims.
Root: The Roleplaying Game, Root Digital, Tabletop Simulator, fiction, recordings, and player sessions.
Named faction labels, Eyrie leader cards, Vagabond character cards/classes, quests, items, and any player-selected story outcomes.
Third and later board-game printings as rules/errata witnesses beyond the documented boundary.
uncertainties: The core box printing number must be read beside its barcode; this pass fixes first printing conceptually but does not claim a particular owned physical copy was inspected.

Leder Games says third printing introduced corrections and minor balance adjustments to faction boards. The current Law of Root has further updates, including rules changed after later expansions/printings; those changes are not applied here.

The product's woodland species/faction imagery and political language are genre/game constructions. The game frames war, extraction, rebellion, monarchy, policing, dominance, and conquest; it should not be treated as a model of real species, peoples, colonial histories, or political movements.
Player choice and asymmetric faction objectives mean individual sessions cannot establish a single canonical winner, alliance, or narrative outcome.
evidence_basis: Official Leder Games product, rules-library, FAQ, and upgrade-kit evidence only. No fan wikis, Wikipedia, play reports, or non-official lore summaries were used.

supports: States that Leder Games released Root in 2018.

citations.locator: A Game of Woodland Might and Right; Asymmetric Design; Resources
supports: Defines the base factions as asymmetric player systems and supplies base-game terms/components.
States that third printing introduced corrections and minor faction-board balance adjustments for first/second-printing owners.

supports: Identifies the current Law as a later rules authority and documents its rules hierarchy.
